page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a multi-core score of 15951.0, both falling into the top 25% tier. It demonstrates strong capabilities in single-threaded gzip compression (33.6 GB/sec), single-threaded bzip3 decompression (13.85 GB/sec), and image processing (13797.0). Cryptographic performance is also notable, with a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 35678.6. For memory-bound tasks, the instance delivers a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 2625.73 GB/sec and an uncached large block read bandwidth of 162.39 GB/sec.

With its dedicated Intel Xeon processor supporting Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), the c7i-flex.8xlarge is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate machine learning inference. It achieves a static web serving throughput of 51.12 GB/sec and processes 135M parameter LLM text generation at 286.26 tokens/sec. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its suitability for high-IOPS database engines or large-scale deep learning training. The flex-class hardware profile offers a balanced, cost-efficient alternative for compute-bound tasks that do not require the full sustained performance of standard compute-optimized instances.
